speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Fourth, make various amendments to clarify and streamline the administration of some parts of the CPF system.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: With this change, members will have three options on their lump-sum withdrawal.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: First, withdraw the lump sum starting from their PEA birthday.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Second, defer withdrawing the lump sum beyond their payout start date for CPF LIFE or the Retirement Sum Scheme by transferring this lump sum to the Ordinary Account.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Third, convert the lump sum into monthly payouts through CPF LIFE or the Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The second amendment simplifies the activation of CPF payouts for members on the Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Today, members who join the CPF LIFE scheme will receive payouts automatically when they reach age 70.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: However, members on the Retirement Sum Scheme have to apply to start their payouts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Some of them may not have done so despite receiving reminders from CPF Board around two months before their PEA.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We are, therefore, amending the CPF Act to allow for automatic starting of payouts at age 70 for members on the Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: This approach is similar to that for CPF LIFE and will start in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The third set of amendments updates the CPF Act to support the implementation of BHS which took effect on 1 January 2016.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The BHS was introduced by MOH for CPF members to meet their basic subsidised healthcare needs in old age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: BHS is fixed for each cohort when they turn 65 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: It is the maximum amount a member can set aside in his MediSave Account.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Any additional MediSave contributions above BHS are transferred to the member's Special or Retirement Accounts to increase his retirement income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In addition, members aged 55 and above now no longer need to top up their MediSave Accounts, before withdrawing from their Ordinary and Special Accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Page: 50 To fully effect these changes, we are amending the CPF Act to remove obsolete provisions relating to the MediSave Minimum Sum and fix the BHS for each cohort when they turn 65 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The fourth and last set of amendments provides greater clarity and efficiency in the administration of some parts of the CPF system and this includes replacing the Minimum Sum with the Retirement Sum, clarifying the administrative financial penalties framework, recovery of Government grants and other payments made in error and catering for members whose birthdays fall on 29 February.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: I will provide just one example on simplifying the MediSave top up process for family members.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Today, members aged 55 and above who have already set aside their cohort Full Retirement Sum have to withdraw the excess monies from their Ordinary and Special Accounts in cash before they can use it to top up the MediSave Account of certain family members aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: The amendment will enable members to make such top ups directly from their Ordinary and Special Accounts to the MediSave Accounts of these family members.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It shows that our Government acts responsibly and responsively.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many Singaporeans were worried that the Minimum Sum is a moving target and they will not be able to reach it when they retire.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Offering different levels of savings on top of the sum also gives members flexibility and choice.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is great news for members who need some extra cash to pursue their interest or dream upon retirement.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I share the Government's constant concern about making Retirement Account savings last.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But I am equally concerned about members' immediate needs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen residents at my Meet-the-People Session, in particular, a resident who lives with her family members, her children's family, and are not happy with the situation and wanted to shift out and buy her own flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: She does not have cash but her money is in her CPF account.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, she says that ""我 只 可 以 看 , 不 可 以 动, 不 可 以 用 " and this is a situation where I feel that perhaps CPF can be more flexible.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is another group of residents who wanted to downgrade, for example, from a 5-room flat to a 3-room flat when they are nearing 55 years old or after 55 years old, but they dare not make the move because they know that the moment they sell the flat, the money will go into CPF Page: 51 Retirement Accounts and that will lock their money up and they cannot buy a smaller flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Indeed, many CPF members were unaware that they previously had to apply for the payout and some were unaware when or how they should do it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Actually, many elderly Singaporeans are oblivious to receiving their GST credits, even after the money had been deposited into their account.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In spite of the letters of notification, some senior citizens are illiterate and do not have children to keep them informed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In the spirit of enabling Singaporeans to make better use of their CPF, I hope CPF Board will make a greater effort to reach out to them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When we introduced MediShield Life, everyone could get free consultations at the Community Centres (CCs) with the help of volunteers from the Insurance and Financial Practitioners Association of Singapore (IFPAS).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: CPF is going to change quite a bit, especially with the second round of recommendations that were released recently.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When all the changes have been finalised, can we also provide such consultations?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   : The CPF amendments will give Singaporeans better peace of mind and more choices as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, when members reach age 70, they can receive payouts automatically without making an application.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the Government has always been concerned about people's livelihood after retirement and has been looking at ways to make Retirement Account savings last longer.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But I am equally concerned about members' immediate needs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some residents have told me that they lived with their children but there were some unpleasant things going on in the family and they wanted to move out and buy their own flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, most of their money is in the CPF; they do not have cash.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This means that they can only "see" the money but are unable to use it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Under the circumstances, I feel that CPF Board should meet people's needs and be more flexible.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Other residents have also told me that they wanted to downgrade, for example, to change to a 3-room flat from a 5-room one.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, they worry that once they sell the flat, the money will be locked up in their CPF account because they are approaching 55 or even older.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If people have money in their CPF account and they need it to buy a flat, CPF Board could perhaps exercise more flexibility in this area to help these residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another suggestion is for CPF Board to make a better effort at explaining to Singaporeans how to use their CPF.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: When we introduced MediShield Life, everyone can get free consultation at the CCs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that after all the changes have been finalised, we can provide similar consultations so that Singaporeans can better Page: 52 understand how to make good use of their CPF monies.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Members are living longer, medical expenses are rising and housing commitments and inflation are factors that may impact our retirement plans in more ways than one.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The latest amendments to the CPF Act are another work in progress to ensure retirement adequacy for members in a changing world.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I hope the CPF Review Panel will continue to make enhancements to the compulsory savings scheme to keep up with the times, the aspirations of our younger workers and the retirement needs of our ageing society.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The new section 18D of the CPF Act is a short addition to the legislation but it carries a significant implication.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The CPF Act, in its current form, already allows members to use their MediSave Account to make payments for medical expenses incurred by other relevant individuals subject to terms and conditions imposed by CPF Board.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: That being the case, what is the main purpose of introducing section 18D of the Bill to allow the topping up of a member's MediSave Account using the Ordinary or Special Account of related members?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Is it to address a concern that the financial adequacy of MediSave Accounts would deteriorate over time, if the same accounts are repeatedly being used to pay for the medical expenses of related persons?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would members, who are unable to tap on their MediSave Account to help their loved ones for whatever reason, be asked to use their Ordinary or Special Account instead, via a transfer made permissible under the new section?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: There is not much detail specified in the new section 18D of the Bill, but, as it stands, such a move will affect the retirement adequacy of members, now that their Ordinary and Special accounts can also be used to top up the MediSave Accounts of their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I seek clarifications on the new section 18D of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But before I end my speech, I wish to ask the Minister to look into enhancing the lump-sum withdrawal option of Retirement Account savings at the PEA in subsequent reviews of the CPF Act.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The decision to delay such withdrawal till PEA was premised on a belief that members would be clearer at that point in time to understand the trade-off between a lump-sum withdrawal of one's retirement savings and lower monthly payouts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: For members with about $80,000 in their Retirement Accounts, it is just a toss between receiving $680 a month or $580 a month with Page: 53 a lump-sum withdrawal of about $20,000.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And such lump-sum withdrawal by members may not relate to financial emergencies as well.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: For members who have set their minds on withdrawing 20% of their Retirement Account savings, what difference does it make to have them withdraw a portion of their CPF savings at age 60, 65, or whatever the PEA may be in the future?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: These members are already mentally prepared for a lower monthly retirement income to begin with, and the illustrative table provided by the CPF Review Report will give them a good gauge of the trade-off involved.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: What these members will stand to lose, however, is the compounded interest on the portion of the retirement savings they wish to take out before attaining PEA, and that may not amount to anything significant, depending on the amount withdrawn.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We can be walking today and bedridden the next.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, using some of our own CPF savings to perform the Haj or fulfil our bucket list of visiting our ancestral village while we are still able to walk is certainly not a luxury but a treat well deserved and a reward well-earned after age 55.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The official Retirement Age does not equate actual retirement age.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Likewise, the re-employment age does not guarantee employment.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: These uncertainties must be reflected in the option to allow members to make partial lump-sum withdrawal of their Retirement Account savings after age 55.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, the CPF system is Singapore's important social security foundation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It has been successfully operating for more than 60 years.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In order to ensure that this system keeps pace with changes, and continue to function effectively, I believe it is necessary to make amendments to the CPF Act.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, we need to take note of two fundamental principles in making amendments to the system.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Essentially, it safeguards the quality of the lifestyle of an individual and that of the household.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: From this perspective, CPF has to adopt a proper and stable management model that is not easily vulnerable to risks.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It is commonly said that "Investment always carries risks and one needs to proceed with caution." There is no business that only earns profits and suffers no losses.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Even the most savvy investor may plunge into losses in a volatile and uncertain market.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: But looking at the 10-year period, Temasek still performs very well Page: 54 overall.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: If even Temasek with its very professional team of researchers could also end up with losses, we cannot expect the small everyday investor to remain unscathed.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, it is critical for the investment of CPF monies to be handled with extreme caution, as this would have a great impact on retirement plans and social stability.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: From a business standpoint, we hope that our employees work very hard when they are young and that they could enjoy their twilight years after retirement.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We do not wish to see our employees liberally use CPF funds to invest, and have this affect their mood and work should they suffer investment losses.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The second principle is that CPF is part of the worker's salary.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Every worker needs to contribute CPF; the employer has to contribute CPF on behalf of his workers, too.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, whether you are a local employer or an overseas investor, CPF contributions should always be taken into account when computing business overheads.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I recall this saying: "The man without thought for the future will surely have trouble close at hand." Presently, Singapore is feeling the impact of a rapidly ageing population.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: If we introduce more flexibility into managing CPF funds and allow people to use their CPF funds for other investment purposes, they may even withdraw their CPF funds completely and spend them when they reach a certain age.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: If the elderly lose their means of financial protection which, in turn, affects social stability, this deviates from the original intention of setting up the CPF scheme.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We need money to sustain our livelihood as we age.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, due to inflation, some elderly people who have reached retirement age have insufficient funds in their CPF to maintain their basic living expenses.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: They have no choice but to continue working to avoid losing the source of income.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This phenomenon should be brought to the attention of the public at large.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Of late, disputes on CPF have become very frequent.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Everyone is expressing concern about the CPF system and safeguards for the elderly.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: CPF is very important to social harmony and stability, and, therefore, the tripartite partners need to review this earnestly.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The Government needs to reflect on the reasons behind the public discontent and decide whether it needs to increase management transparency.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Employers have to make timely contributions to CPF to ensure peace of mind for their employees to do their work.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Employees should also not forget that CPF was set up to provide for their old age.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Most of all, every good system needs to be time-tested.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Having said this, I feel that amendments to the CPF Act should be handled with extreme prudence.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: CPF is a compulsory comprehensive savings plan for working Singaporeans primarily to fund retirement, healthcare and housing needs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It has been a pivotal and integral part of our lives' financial sustainability.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Continuous enhancements of the CPF Act only prove the point that we need to stay relevant to the needs and aspirations of Singaporeans with changing times and evolving lifestyles.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Will the individual or the next-of-kin be allowed an avenue to raise their objections and provide further evidence that it is not the case?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: I have two questions in relation to this clause.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: What are the bases/circumstances to allow a member to transfer the whole or part of the amount in this Ordinary Account?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: While making allowance for flexibility, how does MOM ensure that his/her retirement adequacy is not compromised?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The question is: how could we ensure that employees of such institutions and insurers are given the right understanding and training on the development of schemes, amidst the other schemes provided for the different classes of members?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Even if the penalty is imposed on the institution, there must be safeguards to ensure that financial penalty should not be passed down to the employees who have committed the error.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amendments to the CPF in this Bill will further strengthen the system and have far-reaching implications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I stand in support of this Bill for the following reasons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that we are doing this, as the Minister has mentioned, because some members on the Retirement Sum Scheme may not have made these applications despite receiving repeated reminder letters from CPF Board around two months before their PEA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask if the Board has found out the reasons as to why members did not make these applications?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Was there an increasing number of members who did not make these applications over the past few years?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While this amendment will solve this issue on the surface, I wonder if there are other underlying reasons which we need to look into and address as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Withdrawal of CPF is often a much-awaited event for many retiring Singaporeans who have laboured hard throughout their lives.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the current policy causes a strain on members when they are required to top up their MediSave Accounts before withdrawing from their Ordinary or Special Accounts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This amendment is a step forward to help increase their retirement funds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this period of rising medical costs for our senior citizens, there will be occasions when the balance in their MediSave Accounts runs low and a top up is required.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, this amendment applies to "any person who is related to the member in a manner specified by the Board". "Related Person" is defined in the Act as: (a) his spouse; (b) a child of the member, including an adopted child or a step-child; (c) a father or mother of the member; (d) a brother or sister of the member; (e) a grandchild of the member; (f) a grandparent of the member; or (g) any other person who, in the opinion of the Board, should be regarded as a related person for the purposes of this section.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When interacting with residents, I have encountered many cases of senior citizens being dependent on their sons- or daughters-in-law for their day-to-day needs and they are an integral part of the family.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For some, they could even represent one of the closest members within the family.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify if sons- or daughters-in-law can be classified as a related person under "(g) any other person who in the opinion of the Board should be regarded as a related person for the purposes of this section"?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this period of economic difficulties, Page: 57 Singaporeans will appreciate a more secure safety net for them and their families.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to point out some areas of concern where I feel we should proceed much more cautiously into the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Earlier this year, when the House debated the CPF (Amendment) Bill, there had already been significant discussion of the benefits of the changes then, especially enhanced insurance coverage under the Home Protection Scheme and the greater flexibility afforded by the reduction in requirement for account holders to keep the Full Retirement Sum and, instead, they only need to keep to the lower Basic Retirement Sum.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Although the issue of retirement adequacy had been broached at the time, today's Bill brings the issue into sharper focus because it proposes a scheme for lump-sum withdrawals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: I certainly have no objections to being allowed to make lump-sum withdrawals as an individual.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: But I would like to ask what this will mean, first, for retirement adequacy and, more importantly, for individuals who are looking to such withdrawals possibly as a chance to enjoy a windfall.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: General interest surrounding lump-sum withdrawals has been linked to the issue of individual control over their accounts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: This is an area where I believe more can be done to distinguish between the individual and the collective when it comes to taking responsibility for retirement adequacy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The natural inclination of individual account holders is to want greater flexibility in withdrawal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The challenge, however, is how we deal with the infrequent but inevitable lapses of the very small minority.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Unfortunately, when such lapses occur, for instance, in the form of excessive early withdrawals, it could defeat the effectiveness of CPF for retirement savings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The practice of requiring employers to contribute to the retirement security of their employees is an accepted norm globally, but so is the challenge of ensuring that the monies given over to the control of the beneficiaries are responsibly set aside by the receiving employee.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Whose responsibility is it to ensure retirement adequacy?

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Would allowing lump-sum withdrawals, however limited, from retirement accounts impact on such adequacy?

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The challenge that whoever is responsible for retirement adequacy faces is that the concept itself is not as clearly defined any more, simply because retirement itself seems to be a shifting concept, with different types of workers looking at it differently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Page: 58 While this Bill seeks to provide for account holders to make lump-sum withdrawals under strict conditions, I feel that it should be made clearer that it is not possible for CPF savings to be regarded as a personal bank account.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Too much individual flexibility in handling CPF accounts will compromise its objective of providing blanket retirement adequacy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: We also recognise that CPF can only continue to excel in its core function if it is not loaded with multiple and, sometimes, possibly contradictory objectives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: The well-known trade-off between risks and returns is based on large sample averages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: It should not be mistaken to imply that all individuals who take on higher risks will enjoy higher returns.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: In some cases, the risks will be converted into actual losses and, when these cases hit those who are financially weak, their retirement savings will suffer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Lump-sum withdrawals are no doubt a popular feature, but is it a logical one and what is allowing lump-sum withdrawals meant to achieve?

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Will a lump-sum withdrawal be regarded as a windfall?

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: While such withdrawals will satisfy the individual, it is not necessarily true for the collective.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Allowing CPF accounts to be treated as flexibly as personal bank accounts on one extreme will deplete the pool and reduce its capacity to achieve a good spread of risks.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: It will also directly compromise retirement adequacy and any move in that direction will, unfortunately and ultimately, weaken CPF as an institution in exchange for mere popularity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Moving forward, I believe it would be more important to focus on de-popularising the notion that lump-sum withdrawals can be treated as a windfall, strengthening retirement adequacy, and enhance but also more narrowly target the support for those retirees who are most in need.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Even if we recognise that lump-sum withdrawals require astute management, those who request such a withdrawal will still face the challenge of matching the returns offered by CPF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: Outperforming CPF returns is certainly not something individuals should lightly risk with their retirement funds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: This is a potential new complication, especially since we are talking about limited withdrawals under certain eligibility conditions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
text: By allowing partial withdrawal of a lump sum, does today's Bill imply that the Government is aiming to promote a balance between the two?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I applaud the efforts in this second amendment to automate CPF payouts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will benefit those members who are not on the CPF LIFE scheme but are on the old Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will also benefit those members who are illiterate and those who do not have children or someone to explain the process to them.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Nonetheless, even with simplifications made to CPF, I have met some young people who themselves do not understand how CPF payouts work.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have met residents who came asking for financial help and bitter residents who bemoaned the Government taking their savings when their money was, in fact, sitting in their Retirement Account, waiting to be drawn on.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe this new policy to simplify CPF payouts will be a welcome move.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the topic of simplification, the current CPF scheme, though sound, comprehensive and intricate, can still be seen to be quite complicated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is currently made up of three main accounts – Ordinary Account, Special Account, MediSave Account.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Then, a fourth account, the Retirement Account, is created when the member is 55 years old.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Each account has its own set of processes and benefits.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because the entire scheme is not so simple and challenging to grasp by the layman, a quick search on the Internet reveals several Singaporean blogs and websites proffering help on understanding the whole scheme and advice on optimising the CPF scheme for financial benefit.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some of the advice is sound and others give incorrect information.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Then there are some that exist to incite resentment towards the scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe most of us here are familiar with the "Return Our CPF" saga.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Reasonably, Singaporeans want more transparency about their hard-earned money, and the Government has done its best to make all the information available, even attempting to explain it through case studies, graphics and cartoons.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am especially glad that CPF Board has started a series of roadshows and campaigns to help the people understand and start planning for retirement.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I do hope the public will take advantage of these platforms.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I also hope CPF Board could perhaps explore how it can be even more proactive on an ongoing basis in engaging the public so that the people are kept abreast of its good work and, hopefully, in a simplified way.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It offers greater flexibility in managing money and will be especially handy for those with necessary, large expenses in their old age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   The amendments to the Act this time round also include the option for CPF members to make a lump-sum withdrawal from the Retirement Account.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It offers greater flexibility in managing money and will be especially useful for those who need some large expenses in their old age.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Those who do not have health problems can use the money for self-improvement and learn constructive skills and hobbies that they were not able to learn when they were younger.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I note CPF Board's efforts to use cartoons to explain the CPF system to the public.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is commendable but I believe that the issue of cost had constrained CPF Board from placing more media advertisements.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am not sure if many Singaporeans are aware that this can be done.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should remind CPF members whose spouses are homemakers that they need to do their best to enhance or top up the amount in their spouse's accounts.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This will enable their housewife spouses to Page: 60 become more secure and more comfortable during their retirement.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a good form of savings for old age and can also help the family.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Nonetheless, having such a huge amount of money in hand means there will be many temptations.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is reasonable, of course, to want to pamper yourself with a little reward after working hard for so many years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But expenses meant for enjoyment and comfort, for instance, taking a luxury cruise, buying a new car or renovating your homes – these expenses will build up and the money withdrawn will be gone in a flash.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: For those who plan to invest, be it in the stock market, property or others, please do your research carefully.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Refrain from making high-risk investments if these involve savings that you cannot afford to lose.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Even when buying bonds, one should be careful because we have seen recently how companies are increasingly facing difficulties in fulfilling their obligations and requested for refinancing of payments and others.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Worse still, there are companies that failed or had to close shop altogether.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In English): A point to note is the proliferation of scams from various channels.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To date, several people, including elderly Singaporeans, have fallen prey to such scams and lost huge sums of money, often equating to life savings.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Family members must make efforts to ensure that their elderly relatives, parents and grandparents are aware of these scams.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I hope the Government would do more to reach out to this group of people and generate more awareness.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I know a resident who lives in a 4-room flat.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: She is a single mother and now her children have grown up and moved out of the home.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: She is now the only occupant of the home.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: She has the option to downgrade to a smaller flat and cash out.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Instead, she chose to continue living in her 4-room flat.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As a result, she has to continue working full-time to support her choice.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Above all, remember that you do not need a specific type of property or a certain number of rooms in your house to be happy.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Those who prefer to defer their withdrawals have the additional options of transferring the amounts to the Ordinary Account or converting them into monthly payouts through CPF LIFE or the Retirement Sum Scheme.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is always good to have options to withdraw more and get lower monthly payouts or withdraw less and get higher monthly payouts to cater to different retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is not easy to ensure retirement funding sufficiency while introducing more elements of flexibility in the use of CPF funds.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As it is today, our CPF funds are being used for housing, healthcare, education and investments to a point where, for some members, they do not have enough to fund their retirement expenses, which was the original intent of CPF in the first place.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And, yet, we continue to receive requests to further liberalise the use of CPF funds.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Some argue that the older generation, many of whom are less educated, may need more help from the Government to manage their funds.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: On the other hand, they assert, those in the younger generation are more highly educated and should be empowered to save up for their retirement.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: There is a difference between being more highly educated and financially literate.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It takes knowledge, skills and personal discipline to accumulate funds for the distant future, especially when there are already many current needs and wants.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As years of data have shown, most investors who had used their CPF to invest would have been better off leaving them in the Ordinary Account.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It may be better to err on the side of caution when considering the use of CPF funds for investments by members.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: CPF should remain a low-risk asset for members.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Instead, we should get all members, particularly those from the lower income groups, to focus on building up their CPF accounts.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They should be educated on the power of steady accumulation and compounding, as well as the difference between the interest rates offered by CPF and the banks.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Those seeking employment, including the self-employed, should not be tempted to receive more cash payments upfront in lieu of CPF contributions.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They stand to lose out on Government top ups, if they do not have active CPF accounts and the attractive CPF interest rates.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They should be constantly reminded to contribute to their CPF.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Without funds in their CPF, it would be difficult for them to plan ahead for important milestones, such as buying a home, funding their children's education or be able to afford unexpected medical expenses, let alone fulfil their retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At this point, I would like to commend MOM's public education efforts to increase awareness among workers of their rights.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The recent TV advertisements to inform workers of their entitlements to CPF contributions do a great job in reaching out to workers in an interesting and easy to understand format.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MOM's acronym is particularly suitable for this message – if your employer is not treating you right, just call the hotline and tell MOM!

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Lastly, I would like to voice my support for the amendments to simplify the MediSave top up process for family members.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Currently, there are tax-based incentive schemes to encourage family Page: 62 members to top up the CPF accounts of their loved ones.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The ease of fund transfers will facilitate the strengthening of bonds among family members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I would try to respond to the various points raised according to the four areas of amendments.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: When the CPF Advisory Panel deliberated on this particular recommendation, the views werre divided.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: There were some panel members who felt that we have to continue to tighten on any early withdrawal; while there were others who felt we should provide for flexibility.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, it is a balance between flexibility for early withdrawal versus preserving as much as possible for retirement needs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And we should provide for this early withdrawal not at 55 but at the PEA because, by then, the person would, at the age of 65, for most, be in a better position to look ahead and make the assessment whether he needs more money now or to keep more for retirement years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The comments earlier by the various Members reflect these divided views.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, Mr Png Eng Huat asked, "Why not bring forward to 55?" So, he belongs to the group that goes for flexible provision.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We also have Mr Thomas Chua who reminded the House that we should try to preserve as much as possible for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat likewise called for the public to be cautious.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And last, but not least, we heard the same from Mr Chong Kee Hiong.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CPF Board and MOM are mindful of these divided views.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On balance, we felt that the recommendation by the Advisory Panel was probably the most appropriate one and that is the reason why we are amending the Act to support that.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Louis Ng asked why some members did not activate their Retirement Sum payouts even at the age of 70 and beyond.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CPF Board has been talking to various members and these are the main reasons we have gathered so far.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, they said, "Look, I still have an income, I don't need the money now." They keep it in the Retirement Account.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Some of them have been receiving adequate support from their children.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, they said, "Look, at this moment, I am comfortable with the support.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I don't need to draw on the money." Some of them do not know that they have to Page: 63 activate their payouts under the Retirement Sum Scheme (RSS).

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, they said, "Oh, you mean I have to activate it?" There is yet another group.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Their concern is, "But what if I outlive my Retirement Account savings?" RSS, typically, provides for up to 20 years of payouts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, they said, "Look, I would like to keep it.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I don't know how long I will live.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is better to defer the RSS payouts to as late as possible, just in case I outlive my Retirement Account savings." These are the reasons put forward by the members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For members who, for whatever reason, feel that they still want to defer the start of their payouts, they can do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They can come to CPF Board and we will make sure that they understand how the RSS works, we make sure that they understand the trade-offs between starting their RSS payouts versus deferring it further.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the third area of changes affecting the Basic Healthcare Sum, Ms Thanaletchimi expressed her concern about whether the employees of these medical institutions know what they are doing, after all, there are so many schemes.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Notwithstanding, from time to time, we do discover that they still make mistakes, and this is the reason why we have included this administrative penalty framework, hopefully, to remind them what they have to be more conscious about in filing the claims on behalf of members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Lastly, various amendments about recovering over-payment, payment in error by the Government agencies, I want to explain that members will be served the notice in advance.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CPF Board would not just recover the payment in error without notifying the CPF members.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They would be notified in advance and,if the members have any queries or any objections, they can raise these to CPF Board and then CPF Board will consult the relevant agencies.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Most of these payments made in error did not originate from CPF Board.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are, basically, collecting and making these payments on behalf of the various Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Most of these payments go directly to the households in the form of cheques and into bank accounts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But for cheque payments, if they are not encashed and the cheques expire, then the money is now put into their CPF accounts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is only under these circumstances, if later on, the agencies involved discover that they have made the payment in error, then they will notify CPF Board to recover the money.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As far as CPF recovery is concerned, if the money is still in members' CPF accounts, we will help them to recover.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But if the money is already spent, then it will be beyond the scope of CPF Board.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is to assure Members that there are enough safeguards in place.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the issue of the direct transfer of funds from the Ordinary Account and Special Account to the MediSave Account, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Thanaletchimi asked about who these family members are and who will qualify for this direct transfer to MediSave Account.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: A Member asked whether a son-in-law, daughter-in-law can do the transfer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: If a son-in-law or daughter-in-law wants to top up the parents-in-law's accounts, they are Page: 64 encouraged to do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But if the father-in-law loves his son-in-law so much that he decides to withdraw the money in his CPF account in cash and then give the money to the son-in-law and the son-in-law then puts it back into his MediSave Account, obviously, CPF Board cannot stop it.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This particular amendment is to make it easier for, hopefully, the younger generations to top up the MediSave Accounts of certain family members of the older generations.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Last, but not least, a few Members – Assoc Prof Randolph Tan, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and others – expressed concern that the CPF system is getting too complicated and sometimes members are finding it difficult to decide at which point in time to do what.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In fact, that is the reason why CPF Board is now mounting another exercise to try and explain the CPF system in a simpler way, in a way that, hopefully, more members will be able to have a better appreciation.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I did a trial run with a few hundred grassroots leaders just about two weeks ago, putting it in a very simple way.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Quite a number of them feel that they are now more confident to help us explain the CPF system to members of the public.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are going to conduct a few more sessions in Tamil, Malay and Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: After this series of four sessions, we are going to take stock based on the feedback and see how can we refine it further and, beyond that, I want to go back to all the Grassroots Advisers to help us send out the message.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At the same time, I also want to add that one of the key concerns that we have is about retirement planning.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In this regard, I am happy to say that CPF Board had, in the second half of last year, piloted a retirement planning service.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: CPF Board is also exploring the possibility of doing a similar exercise to reach out to members on a one-on-one basis upon reaching the PEA.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, we will step up our efforts of engagement broadly in the community and, at the same time, individually, at the key milestone of age 55 and the PEA of individual members.
